newsitem.title: UK: UK health minister backtracks on Scottish row.
newsitem.headline: UK health minister backtracks on Scottish row.

text.p: Health Minister Stephen Dorrell fought on Monday to defuse a row about an interview in which he apparently promised a future Conservative administration would abolish any Scottish parliament set up by a Labour government.
Dorrell told The Scotsman newspaper: "Clearly, institutional arrangements which damage the union of the UK are not something a later Conservative government would leave unchanged."

The remark was immediately seized on by opposition parties, who said it was insulting to Scotland and at odds with the views of the ruling party's Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth, who has said the Conservatives would not reverse any devolution introduced in Scotland by a Labour government.

But Dorrell said in a statement on Monday: "I told The Scotsman that in the unlikely event of the country being misguided enough to elect a Labour government and a Scottish parliament being set up, the Conservatives would, of course, stand for election to it..."

"I also made it clear in my interview that I was not willing to speculate about a hypothetical question of what a Conservative government, two parliaments down the line from here, might do if it comes to office and found a Scottish parliament in existence," he said.

"I did say that any Conservative government which came to office and found arrangements in place which damaged the constitution could not leave them unchanged. That is not the same as saying it would abolish such a parliament and there us no difference between myself and Michael Forsyth on this issue."
But opposition parties, sensing a political gaffe by Dorrell, pounced on his remarks.

Labour's Scottish spokesman George Robertson said: "This gaffe is a humiliating slap in the face for the Scottish Secretary, who has repeatedly said that the Tories will not abolish a devolved parliament if it has been established."

Scottish National Party leader Alex Salmond added: "The Tories (Conservatives) are in a state of total disarray on the Scottish constitution, but Stephen Dorrell has given their real intentions in Scotland away."
Dorrell, a close ally of Prime Minister John Major, has been given the job of fighting Labour's devolution ideas in the run-up to the election, now no more than three months away.
But the Conservatives are floundering in their attempts to combat Labour, which remains around 20 points ahead in polls. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
